S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by marked, persistent fear or anxiety about a clearly defined object or situation that is out of proportion to actual danger and leads to avoidance or significant distress and impairment. The fear response is typically immediate and consistent when the person encounters, or anticipates encountering, the phobic trigger, and the person often recognizes that the fear is excessive or unreasonable. Onset can occur in childhood or adulthood and the course is often chronic if untreated, though individuals may function well in other areas of life except where the phobic cue is involved. It is distinguished from social anxiety disorder and agoraphobia by the narrow, circumscribed nature of the feared stimulus and from PTSD or OCD by the absence of broader trauma-related syndromes or intrusive obsessions/compulsions driving the avoidance.

patient.personality: Joby is a laid-back but meticulous hands-on craftsman who enjoys mentoring others, spending time outdoors, and improvising solutions on the job and in his hobbies.
patient.stressor: About a year ago, Joby was installing custom cabinets on a second-floor renovation when a temporary railing failed and a coworker slipped, nearly pulling Joby over the edge before another crew member grabbed him; the coworker suffered a serious injury and Joby was left shaken by how close he’d come to falling. In the weeks that followed, he tried to push through and keep working on similar jobs, but he found himself increasingly tense whenever he had to work near exposed edges or climb certain types of ladders, quietly trading tasks with apprentices or reassigning himself to ground-level work. Over the next 11 months, this pattern hardened into a consistent avoidance of particular job sites and tasks, forcing him to turn down higher-paying framing and roofing work and rely more on shop-based projects, which strained his income and his sense of competence as a full-service carpenter. He finally sought psychiatric help after his boss warned him that his refusal to take on certain standard site assignments was jeopardizing both current contracts and his role as a mentor to apprentices.
patient.chief_complaint: “Whenever I have to get back into that kind of spot at work, it hits me right away and I just freak out inside.”

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: Ever since that accident, any time I’m up near an open edge or on one of those taller ladders, it feels like my body is convinced I’m about to pitch over the side even if it’s only a ten-foot drop and there’s a perfectly good guardrail there.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If I even picture myself standing on a roof or looking down from a second-floor balcony, my chest tightens, my hands get sweaty, and my legs go kind of rubbery, and if I’m actually up there it hits me in a split second like my whole system slams on the brakes.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I go out of my way to avoid jobs that mean working high up—swapping tasks, making excuses to stay in the shop, or, if I can’t get out of it, hugging the wall or crawling instead of walking normally while my heart’s pounding the whole time.
